name: Copper
summary: Contrasting case: highest performance with almost no controllability. Copper is included in the data set deliberately, because a controllability schema is worthless if it cannot also show where there is nothing to control. The only interesting variable is catalytic, not electronic.

degrees_of_freedom.description: Can only be changed via temperature and purity, not switched
Crystal facet of the surface; determines the product selectivity of CO2 reduction

validity.condition: Linearization about 293 K with alpha = 0.00393 /K and sigma(293 K) = 5.96e7 S/m

couplings.source: Hori et al., J. Mol. Catal. A 199, 39 (2003); overview of metal selectivities in Hori et al., Electrochim. Acta 39, 1833 (1994)
couplings.notes: Copper is the only metal with appreciable C-C coupling in CO2 reduction. The selectivity depends strongly on potential and facet, but not monotonically.

couplings.source: Hori, Takahashi, Koga & Hoshi, J. Mol. Catal. A 199, 39 (2003), doi:10.1016/S1381-1169(03)00016-5
couplings.notes: Exactly the edge whose refinement a QPU calculation would have to deliver. Currently low, because classical DFT does not reliably resolve the reaction network. The value for oxide-derived copper is conservative: modern gas diffusion electrodes reach 70 to 90 percent Faradaic efficiency towards C2+.

gaps: No switchable electronic degree of freedom. Copper is deliberately edge-poor in the schema.
The facet dependence of CO2 reduction is quantitatively uncertain; the values are indicative, not target figures.
The origin of the Cu(211) value of 0.25 could not be traced back to a primary source.
